title: Analytical modelling of food storage cooling with solar ammonia-water absorption system
author: Pop, Dobrovicescu, et al.
materials: The main refrigerating circuit is composed of the condenser, the expansion device, the evaporator, and the heat exchanger, while the thermochemical compressor consists of the following components: absorber; rich solution pump; generator; expansion device of the weak solution and heat exchanger. The refrigerant is NH3 and the solvent is H2O. The working process of the main refrigerating circuit is presented in Fig. 4 in the pressure – enthalpy diagram, while the working process of the NH3—H2O solution is presented in Fig. 5 in the enthalpy – concentration diagram.Fig. 4The working process of the main refrigerating circuit.Fig 4Fig. 5The working process of the NH3—H2O solution.Fig 5

steps.title: Define Storage and Product Parameters
steps.instruction: Establish the operational parameters for the four food storage types using chicken meat as the product.

substeps.instruction: Set inside temperature (ti) to 3 °C for Refrigeration Chamber (RC) and Refrigerated Storage (RS), and -20 °C for Freezing Chamber (FC) and Frozen Storage (FS).
Set inside relative humidity to 90% for all cases.
Define ventilation air flow rate as 3 storage volumes in 24 h (15,000 m3/h).
Specify wall construction as sandwich panels filled with polyurethane, calculated for ambient conditions of 40 °C and 40% relative humidity.

steps.title: Calculate Time-Variant Cooling Loads
steps.instruction: Determine the total cooling load by calculating the individual heat gain components.

substeps.instruction: Calculate cooling load through walls (Qw) using Qw = k·S·(tdb - ti), where k·S values are 0.0135 kW/K (RC), 0.676 kW/K (RS), 0.0083 kW/K (FC), and 0.50 kW/K (FS).
Calculate ventilation cooling load (Qv) for RS using Qv = ρ·V˙·c·(tdb - ti).

Calculate technological cooling load (Qt) for chicken meat using Qt = a·τ² - b·τ + c, with coefficients from Table 4 (Refrigeration: a=0.21, b=204.306, c=1521.9990; Freezing: a=0.08, b=133.116, c=6529.8795).
Determine operation cooling load (Qop) as 40% of the wall cooling load: Qop = 0.4 · Qw.

steps.title: Model Cooling Tower Thermal Regime
steps.instruction: Determine the cooling water temperature (tw) based on ambient conditions.

substeps.instruction: Calculate wet bulb temperature (twb) using the provided equation (Eq. 7) based on dry bulb temperature (tdb) and relative humidity (φ).
Calculate cooling water return temperature as tw = twb + 5 °C.
Adjust fan speed to maintain a minimum cooling water outlet temperature of 10 °C.

steps.title: Model Heat Storage Tank Behavior
steps.instruction: Simulate the thermal buffer using diathermic oil to power the absorption plant during low solar radiation.

substeps.instruction: Set oil specific heat capacity (c) to 1.85 kJ/kgK.
Apply polyurethane thermal insulation with a thickness of 0.5 m.
Calculate temperature variation (Δt) using Δt = Qst / (m·c), where Qst is the balance of solar excess heat, extracted heat, and insulation losses.
Set maximum oil temperature to either the required hot temperature or 400 °C.

steps.title: Analyze Absorption Refrigeration Plant
steps.instruction: Determine the internal working conditions and performance of the NH3-H2O one-stage absorption system.

substeps.instruction: Set evaporating temperature: t0 = ti - 13 °C.
Set condensing temperature: tk = tw + 8 °C.
Set saturated weak solution temperature: tg = th - 10 °C (where th is hot oil temperature).
Set superheated refrigerant temperature: t8 = tk - 20 °C.
Calculate specific enthalpies (h5, h6, h10, h11, h12, hPi) and recirculating factor (f) using the provided energy balance and concentration equations (Eq. 14-22).
Compute specific thermal powers for the absorber (qAb), rectifier (qR with ηr = 0.88), generator (qG), condenser (qk), and evaporator (q0).
Calculate COP as the ratio of q0 to qG.

steps.title: Determine Solar Field Temperature Limits
steps.instruction: Calculate the minimum required hot temperature (th) at the SPTC outlet to maintain the degassing zone (Δξ).

substeps.instruction: Use the relation th = a·tw + b based on the chosen degassing zone (Δξ = 0.06 or 0.1) and regime (Refrigeration or Freezing) using coefficients from Table 5.

steps.title: Evaluate Backup Mechanical Refrigeration
steps.instruction: Model the electrical backup system using NH3 as the refrigerant.

substeps.instruction: Calculate the COP of the mechanical compression cycle using the correlation COP = e·tw² + f·tw + g with coefficients from Table 7.

steps.title: Implement Mathematical Model
steps.instruction: Integrate all component models into computational software.

substeps.instruction: Implement the equations in Engineering Equation Solver (EES) and Microsoft Excel.
